title: Billing Team Worksheet: Monthly Installment Amount on the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
**Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program — billing team worksheet: the monthly installment of an interest-free payment plan**

This worksheet figures the monthly installment of an interest-free payment plan that a customer accepts on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment. The installment is the plan balance divided by the number of installments, rounded to the nearest cent, a half cent going to the even cent, in USD with 2 decimal places. The quantities that enter it are defined below in the terms of the enrollment's records.

## 1. The program's unpaid balance

The program's unpaid balance is the remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds posted on it less the payments and balance adjustments posted on it: the total of the patient responsibility left by the payer remittances, the patient charges and the patient refunds posted on the enrollment's billing ledger, less the total of the patient payments and the balance adjustments posted on that ledger.

## 2. Terms of the patient account

- *Recent postings* are those posted less than one whole calendar month before today: a posting is recent when the whole calendar months from its posting date to today are 0. A program's recent remittances are the patient responsibility left by the payer remittances recently posted on its billing ledger, and its recent patient charges are the patient charges recently posted on that ledger.
- *Whole calendar months* from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day.
- *The same coverage record.* The customer's Insulin Pump Program bills the same coverage record when it is not closed and its coverage record is the one the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment bills. Not closed is any status other than closed; a customer who holds no Insulin Pump Program has none that bills the same coverage record.

## 3. The plan balance

The plan balance is the program's unpaid balance, never below zero, rounded to the nearest cent, a half cent going to the even cent. An unpaid balance of zero or less gives a plan balance of 0.00.

## 4. The number of installments

A plan priced on this worksheet runs for the tier's longest payment plan, in monthly installments, as the tier's payment plan schedule states it for the tier the enrollment holds.

## 5. The installment

Each installment is the plan balance divided by the installments, rounded to the nearest cent, a half cent going to the even cent: an amount lying exactly halfway between two cents goes to the one whose last digit is even.

## 6. How the figures combine

Each adjustment changes the plan balance or the installment figured above as that adjustment states, in this order: amounts taken off another program's postings come off only the amount added from that program, never taking it below zero; every other addition and deduction is then applied to the plan balance; and the installment is figured and rounded last.

No plan is priced, and the installment is 0.00, when the tier's longest payment plan is 0 installments, when the plan balance so reached is below the tier's payment plan minimum balance, or when the installment would be below the tier's payment plan minimum installment. A plan balance exactly equal to the minimum balance, or an installment exactly equal to the minimum installment, is not below it. Amounts are in USD with 2 decimal places.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

Every figure below is a hypothetical input chosen for illustration; none is a tier figure. Suppose the tier's longest payment plan were 8 installments, its payment plan minimum balance 130.00 and its payment plan minimum installment 18.00.

| Hypothetical ledger | Plan balance | Divided by 8 | Installment |
|---|---|---|---|
| remittance patient responsibility 412.30, patient charges 95.90; payments 150.00, balance adjustments 20.00 | 338.20 | 42.275 | 42.28 (halfway; 28 is even) |
| postings netting to 338.12 | 338.12 | 42.265 | 42.26 (halfway; 26 is even) |
| postings netting to 144.00 | 144.00 | 18.00 | 18.00 (equal to the minimum installment, so priced) |
| postings netting to 140.00 | 140.00 | 17.50 | 0.00 (below the minimum installment) |
| postings netting to 129.99 | 129.99 | — | 0.00 (below the minimum balance) |
| payments exceeding the postings by 12.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 (below the minimum balance) |

In the first row the unpaid balance is 412.30 plus 95.90, less 150.00 and less 20.00, which is 338.20; 338.20 divided by 8 is 42.275, exactly halfway between 42.27 and 42.28, and goes to the even cent, 42.28.

Had the tier's longest payment plan been 0 installments, every row would give 0.00.
